key_insight: Population-based reference equations contextualize neurodegeneration blood biomarkers using individualized expected concentrations, percentiles, and Z-scores.
clinical_relevance: This neurodegeneration study—not AI cancer drug discovery—offers a framework for interpreting biomarker levels while accounting for physiological differences.
method: Analyzed plasma from cognitively unimpaired participants in two French population cohorts.
Modeled six biomarkers and their ratios using age, sex, body-mass index, and renal function.
Evaluated disease-associated Z-score profiles and developed NfL cross-calibration equations across methods and sample matrices.
evidence_signal: Reference populations included 5,122–5,123 participants; expected NfL and GFAP increased with age, disease-associated profiles were preserved, and NfL cross-calibration achieved intraclass correlations above 0.90.
watch_item: The cross-sectional French reference populations may limit generalizability; broader validation is needed before routine clinical implementation.
paper_title: Population-based reference equations and Z-scores for blood biomarkers of neurodegenerative diseases
